definitions.explanation: An egg fried in a pan without flipping, so the yolk remains visible on top. The name literally means 'eyeball fry' because the round yolk resembles an eye.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}ごはん⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{目玉焼|めだまや}き⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}った→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: I made a fried egg for breakfast.

examples.japanese: {目玉焼|めだまや}き⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{醤油|しょうゆ}→醤油：01056_shouyu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦かける→かける：00854_kakeru⟧⟦{派|は}→派：28356_ha⟧です⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧。
examples.english: Are you the type to put soy sauce on your fried egg?

examples.japanese: ⟦{半熟|はんじゅく}→半熟：11935_hanjuku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{目玉焼|めだまや}き⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{乗|の}せた→乗せる：01972_noseru⟧⟦ハンバーグ→ハンバーグ：01785_hanbaagu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{人気|にんき}→人気：01488_ninki⟧⟦メニュー→メニュー：11166_menyuu⟧だ。
examples.english: A hamburger steak topped with a soft-fried egg is a popular menu item.

notes:
A staple of Japanese home cooking and cafe menus. The name comes from ⟦{目玉|めだま}→目玉：13649_medama⟧ (eyeball) + ⟦{焼|や}き→焼く：01123_yaku⟧ (fried), describing the appearance of the round yolk.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {目玉焼|めだまや}き⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{焼|や}く→焼く：01123_yaku⟧ (to fry an egg)
- ⟦{半熟|はんじゅく}→半熟：11935_hanjuku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{目玉焼|めだまや}き (soft-fried egg with runny yolk)
- {目玉焼|めだまや}き{丼|どん} (fried egg rice bowl)

CULTURAL NOTE:
What to put on a {目玉焼|めだまや}き is a common topic of friendly debate in Japan. Some prefer ⟦{醤油|しょうゆ}→醤油：01056_shouyu⟧ (soy sauce), others ⟦{塩|しお}→塩：00887_shio⟧ (salt), ⟦ソース→ソース：17673_soosu⟧ (Worcestershire sauce), or ⟦ケチャップ→ケチャップ：14719_kechappu⟧ (ketchup).
